title: Semantic search
content: Semantic search is search that matches a query to content by meaning and intent in place of exact shared words.

meta.why: A page that explains a subject in plain terms can match questions phrased in several ways, including ones that share none of its exact words.
meta.example: A search for ways to stop cart abandonment returns a page whose title talks about checkout drop-off.
meta.check: List the different ways buyers phrase one question and confirm the page answers that question in plain language.
meta.limitation: Semantic matching finds related content and does not judge whether the content is correct.
meta.sources: Google Cloud: what is semantic search | https://cloud.google.com/discover/what-is-semantic-search | Platform documentation
